rules.statement: The annual accounts shall give, in accordance with norms acceptable in society, such insight that a reasoned judgment can be formed about the financial position and result of the legal entity (true-and-fair view).
The balance sheet with notes shall faithfully, clearly and consistently present the size and composition of the entity's assets and liabilities at year-end.
The profit-and-loss account with notes shall faithfully, clearly and consistently present the size of the result of the financial year and its derivation from income and expense items.

If compliance with the statutory layout and valuation requirements is insufficient to give the required true-and-fair view, additional information must be provided in the notes (and a justified departure made where necessary).
The annual accounts shall be drawn up in euros and in the Dutch language, unless another currency or language is justified by the nature of the entity (verify).
Items in the balance sheet and profit-and-loss account shall not be netted unless permitted, and each item shall be shown separately with corresponding prior-year comparatives.

The balance sheet shall present assets split into vaste activa (fixed assets) and vlottende activa (current assets), and the credit side into eigen vermogen, voorzieningen and schulden, in the statutory order.
Vaste activa shall be subdivided into immateriële vaste activa, materiële vaste activa and financiële vaste activa.
Immateriële vaste activa shall separately disclose, among others, costs of development, concessions/licences/intellectual property, goodwill paid, and prepayments on intangibles (verify).
Materiële vaste activa shall be subdivided into, among others, land and buildings, plant and machinery, other operating assets, and assets under construction / prepayments.
Financiële vaste activa shall separately disclose participating interests, receivables from group companies and participations, other securities and other receivables.
Vlottende activa shall be subdivided into voorraden (inventories), vorderingen (receivables), effecten (securities) and liquide middelen (cash) (verify).

Voorzieningen (provisions) may only be recognised for liabilities/losses whose existence is certain or probable at balance date but whose amount or timing is uncertain, and shall be measured at best estimate (verify).
Eigen vermogen shall be split into issued capital, share premium (agio), revaluation reserve, other statutory and articles-of-association reserves, and retained/undistributed result.
Schulden (liabilities) shall be classified by type and disclose separately the portion with a remaining term exceeding one year and that exceeding five years.

The profit-and-loss account shall be presented in one of the statutory models (categorical/type-of-expense model or functional/cost-of-sales model) showing net turnover, operating expenses, financial income/expense and result.
Income and expenses arising from events not belonging to ordinary activities shall be disclosed by nature and amount in the notes (verify).

Assets and liabilities shall be measured on the basis of historical cost (verkrijgings-/vervaardigingsprijs) or current value (actuele waarde), and the chosen valuation grondslagen shall be disclosed and applied consistently.

Valuation and result determination shall apply prudence; only profits realised at balance date may be recognised, while foreseeable liabilities and losses originating in the financial year shall be taken into account.
Valuation shall assume continuity of the entity (going concern) unless that assumption is no longer warranted (verify).
Where current value is used, the applicable form (replacement value, market value, realisable value or value in use) shall be applied and a revaluation reserve maintained where required.

Fixed assets with limited useful life shall be depreciated/amortised systematically over their useful life; impairments of fixed and current assets shall be recognised when their value is expected to be permanently/durably lower (verify).
An asset shall be carried at the lower of cost and recoverable amount when a durable (lasting) impairment applies; the impairment is reversed when the reasons for it cease to exist.

Micro legal entities (not exceeding two of: balance total EUR 450,000; net turnover EUR 900,000; 10 employees) may file a strongly simplified balance sheet and are exempt from a profit-and-loss account and notes.

Small legal entities (not exceeding two of: balance total EUR 7,500,000; net turnover EUR 15,000,000; 50 employees) may prepare and file abridged accounts, are exempt from audit and from a management report.
Medium-sized legal entities (not exceeding two of: balance total EUR 25,000,000; net turnover EUR 50,000,000; 250 employees) may apply specified disclosure exemptions but must be audited.
Size classification shall be based on the criteria on two consecutive balance dates before a different size regime may be applied (verify).
The annual accounts shall be filed with the Chamber of Commerce (KvK) within 8 days of adoption, and ultimately within 12 months of the financial year-end.
Management shall prepare the annual accounts within 5 months of year-end (extendable by up to 5 months by the general meeting), after which adoption by the general meeting follows (verify).
Legal entities that are not small must have their annual accounts audited by a registered (RA/AA) external auditor who issues an audit opinion.
The management report (bestuursverslag) shall give a fair review of the entity's situation, development and expected course of affairs, consistent with the annual accounts.

Revenue from the sale of goods/services shall be recognised when the economic benefits are realisable (the amount can be measured reliably and inflow is probable) and earned (significant risks and rewards transferred).
An entity acting as principal recognises gross revenue, whereas an entity acting as agent recognises only the net commission/fee earned (verify).
Revenue and result on construction/onderhanden projecten shall be recognised by stage of completion (percentage-of-completion) where the outcome can be estimated reliably.
Inventories (voorraden) shall be measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value (opbrengstwaarde).
Inventory cost shall be assigned using FIFO or weighted-average cost; LIFO is not permitted (verify).
Development costs may be capitalised as an intangible asset when defined criteria are met; research costs shall always be expensed.
When development costs are capitalised, a legal reserve (wettelijke reserve) equal to the unamortised carrying amount must be maintained within equity and is not distributable.
The estimated useful life over which an intangible fixed asset is amortised shall not exceed twenty years (verify).
General-ledger accounts should be mapped to standardised RGS reference codes to enable uniform exchange and SBR reporting to KvK, Belastingdienst and CBS.
Each RGS account carries a hierarchical reference code and a unique RGS number that maps one-to-one to the corresponding SBR taxonomy element (verify).
Statutory KvK deposit of accounts for micro and small entities is performed via SBR (XBRL) instances built on the RGS/NT taxonomy (verify).
Every merchant (Kaufmann) shall keep books and record their commercial transactions and the state of their assets in accordance with the Grundsätze ordnungsmäßiger Buchführung (GoB).

At the start of business and at the end of each financial year the merchant shall prepare a balance sheet (Bilanz) and, additionally, a profit-and-loss account (Gewinn- und Verlustrechnung) forming the Jahresabschluss.
The Jahresabschluss shall be drawn up in accordance with GoB and be clear and well-arranged (klar und übersichtlich) within the prescribed period.
The Jahresabschluss shall be prepared in German and in euros.

The Jahresabschluss shall include all assets, liabilities, accruals/deferrals, expenses and income (completeness), and items shall not be offset against each other (Saldierungsverbot / gross principle).
Self-created intangible fixed assets may be capitalised at development cost (Aktivierungswahlrecht); research costs and self-created brands/mastheads/customer lists may not be capitalised.

Valuation shall be prudent (Vorsichtsprinzip): all foreseeable risks and losses up to the balance-sheet date shall be recognised, and only profits realised at the balance-sheet date may be reported (Realisationsprinzip).
Valuation shall assume continuation of the business activity (going concern) unless actual or legal circumstances oppose it.
Assets and liabilities shall be valued individually (Einzelbewertung) at the balance-sheet date.
Expenses and income of the financial year shall be accounted for irrespective of the dates of the corresponding payments (accrual / Periodenabgrenzung).
Valuation methods applied in the prior annual financial statements shall be retained (Bewertungsstetigkeit / consistency).
Assets shall be carried at no more than acquisition or production cost (Anschaffungs-/Herstellungskosten) reduced by depreciation/amortisation; liabilities at their settlement amount.
Current assets (Umlaufvermögen) shall be written down to the lower stock-exchange/market value or attributable value at the balance-sheet date (strenges Niederstwertprinzip).
Fixed assets (Anlagevermögen) shall be written down to the lower attributable value on a permanent impairment (gemildertes Niederstwertprinzip; mandatory only if durable).
A prior write-down shall be reversed (Wertaufholungsgebot) if the reasons for it no longer apply, except for goodwill.
Acquisition cost comprises purchase price plus incidental acquisition costs less reductions; production cost comprises direct material/labour and special direct costs plus permitted overheads.

The balance sheet shall be presented in account form (Kontoform) with assets ordered Anlagevermögen then Umlaufvermögen, and equity-and-liabilities ordered Eigenkapital, Rückstellungen, Verbindlichkeiten, in the prescribed sequence.
Small corporations need only present a balance sheet limited to the items designated with letters and Roman numerals (abridged balance sheet).

Eigenkapital shall be broken down into subscribed capital (gezeichnetes Kapital), capital reserve (Kapitalrücklage), revenue reserves (Gewinnrücklagen), retained earnings/loss carried forward and net income/loss for the year (verify).
The profit-and-loss account shall be presented in vertical/staggered form (Staffelform) using either the total-cost method or the cost-of-sales method.
Under the total-cost method (Gesamtkostenverfahren), expenses are classified by nature (material, personnel, depreciation) and changes in inventory and own work capitalised are shown separately.
Under the cost-of-sales method (Umsatzkostenverfahren), expenses are classified by function (cost of goods sold, distribution, administration).

The annual accounts of a corporation shall, observing GoB, give a true and fair view (ein den tatsächlichen Verhältnissen entsprechendes Bild) of the assets, financial and earnings position, supplemented by a Anhang (notes).
Corporations are classified small/medium/large by exceeding at least two of three criteria (balance-sheet total, revenue, average employees) on two consecutive balance-sheet dates.
A small corporation does not exceed two of: balance-sheet total EUR 7,500,000; revenue EUR 15,000,000; 50 average employees (thresholds raised for financial years beginning after 31 Dec 2023).
A medium-sized corporation does not exceed two of: balance-sheet total EUR 25,000,000; revenue EUR 50,000,000; 250 average employees.
A micro corporation does not exceed two of: balance-sheet total EUR 450,000; revenue EUR 900,000; 10 average employees, and may apply further presentation and disclosure simplifications.
The annual accounts and management report of corporations that are not small shall be audited by a statutory auditor (Abschlussprüfer); without audit the accounts cannot be adopted.
Corporations shall disclose their annual accounts no later than one year after the financial-year balance-sheet date (filed with the Unternehmensregister / formerly Bundesanzeiger).
Accounting books, inventories, opening balance sheets and annual accounts shall be retained for 10 years, and commercial correspondence for 6 years (verify).
SKR03 is a process-oriented (Prozessgliederung) standard chart of accounts numbering accounts along the business process cycle; it is widely used for HGB bookkeeping.
SKR04 is a financial-statement-oriented (Abschlussgliederung) standard chart of accounts whose account ranges follow the HGB §266/§275 balance-sheet and P&L structure.
In SKR04, account class 0 covers fixed assets/equity, class 1 financial assets and current assets, class 2 equity & provisions, class 3 liabilities, classes 4-7 income/expenses (verify).
The annual accounts (comptes annuels) shall be regular, sincere and give a faithful image (image fidèle) of the entity's assets, financial position and result (verify).
Accounting shall apply the principle of prudence (prudence): assets and income are not overstated and liabilities and charges are not understated (verify).
Assets shall in principle be recorded at historical cost (coût historique): acquisition cost for purchased assets and production cost for produced assets (verify).
Accounts shall be prepared on a going-concern basis (continuité d'exploitation) (verify).
Charges and income shall be attached to the financial year to which they relate (indépendance/spécialisation des exercices) (verify).
Methods of presentation and valuation shall be applied consistently from one period to the next (permanence des méthodes) (verify).
Account class 1 (comptes de capitaux) records equity, reserves, results, regulated provisions, borrowings and similar long-term liabilities.
Account class 2 (comptes d'immobilisations) records intangible, tangible and financial fixed assets and their depreciation/amortisation and impairment.
Account class 3 (comptes de stocks et en-cours) records inventories and work-in-progress.
Account class 4 (comptes de tiers) records receivables and payables: suppliers, customers, personnel, social bodies, the State (incl. TVA) and other third parties.
Account class 5 (comptes financiers) records bank accounts, cash, marketable securities and other treasury movements.
Account class 6 (comptes de charges) records expenses by nature: operating, financial and exceptional charges plus income tax.
Account class 7 (comptes de produits) records income by nature: operating, financial and exceptional income.
Account class 8 (comptes spéciaux) records off-balance-sheet commitments and other special items (verify).
The plan de comptes is common to the base, abridged and developed systems; numbering follows the decimal logic of the seven classes.
Small entities meeting the thresholds may present the balance sheet and income statement under the abridged system (système abrégé) (verify).
The base system (système de base) provides the standard balance-sheet (in table form) and income-statement (in list form) models for entities above the abridged thresholds (verify).
The developed system (système développé) provides additional management-oriented presentation; its separate balance-sheet/income-statement models were removed by the PCG modernisation (verify).

The balance sheet (bilan) shall present, on the asset side, fixed assets (actif immobilisé) and current assets (actif circulant), and on the liability side equity (capitaux propres), provisions and liabilities (dettes) (verify).
The income statement (compte de résultat) shall distinguish operating result (résultat d'exploitation), financial result and exceptional result, presented in list form (verify).
The annual accounts shall include an annexe (notes) completing and commenting on the balance sheet and income statement; very small entities may be exempt (verify).
Development costs may be capitalised as an intangible asset when the conditions are met; research costs are expensed (verify).
Inventories shall be valued at acquisition or production cost; a depreciation (dépréciation) is recognised when the net realisable value is lower (verify).

rules.source: LPF art. L47 A / art. A47 A-1 CGI (verify)
rules.statement: Entities keeping computerised accounts shall be able to produce the Fichier des Écritures Comptables (FEC), a dematerialised file of all accounting entries, on a tax audit (verify).
The FEC shall contain the prescribed 18 fields per entry, including JournalCode, EcritureNum, EcritureDate, CompteNum, PieceRef, Debit, Credit and lettrage (verify).
Every accounting entry in the FEC shall be balanced (total debit equals total credit) and chronologically and immutably recorded (verify).

rules.source: Code de commerce art. L232-21 et seq. (verify)
rules.statement: Companies shall file their approved annual accounts with the registry of the commercial court (greffe du tribunal de commerce) within one month of approval (two months if filed electronically) (verify).
Small companies may request that their filed accounts (or income statement) remain confidential and not be made public, within the statutory size limits (verify).

rules.source: Code de commerce art. L823-1 / L221-9 (verify)
rules.statement: Appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory when a company exceeds two of: balance-sheet total EUR 5,000,000; revenue EUR 10,000,000; 50 employees (verify).
Accounting documents and supporting vouchers shall be retained for 10 years (verify).
Issuers with securities admitted to trading on an EU regulated market shall prepare their annual financial report in the XHTML format.
Issuers preparing IFRS consolidated financial statements shall mark them up with Inline XBRL (iXBRL) tags from the ESEF taxonomy.
Primary financial statements (financial position, profit or loss, comprehensive income, cash flows, changes in equity) shall be tagged in detail at individual-value level.
The notes to the IFRS consolidated statements shall be block-tagged at section level (mandatory for financial years beginning on or after 1 Jan 2022) (verify).
Where no core ESEF taxonomy element matches a disclosed item, the issuer shall create an extension (custom) element and anchor it to the closest standard element(s) (verify).
ESEF tagging applies only to issuers whose securities are admitted to trading on an EU regulated market; non-listed entities are out of scope.
A SAF-T file shall contain a Header group with company identification, fiscal/selection period, currency, taxonomy/schema version and producing-software details.
A SAF-T file shall contain a GeneralLedgerAccounts master-file group listing each ledger account with its ID, description, type and opening/closing balances.
A SAF-T file shall contain Customers and Suppliers master-file groups with party identification, tax registration (VAT) number, address and balances.
A SAF-T file shall contain a TaxTable master-file group defining the tax (VAT) codes, rates and descriptions referenced by the entries.
A SAF-T file shall contain a GeneralLedgerEntries group of journals and transaction lines, each line carrying account, date, debit/credit amount and document references.
A SAF-T file should contain a SourceDocuments group with sales/purchase invoices, payments and movement-of-goods records linking source documents to ledger entries.
A SAF-T export shall be a valid XML document conforming to the applicable national SAF-T XSD schema version (verify).
